points.description: States that the address-of operator (&) returns the memory address (location in memory) of its operand (the variable/object it is applied to).
points.partial_credit: 2 marks if vague or half right, e.g. says it returns the 'address' or 'location' without saying memory/of the operand, or mentions a pointer without making clear it is the operand's address.

points.description: Makes clear the address returned belongs to the operand (the variable it is applied to), not its value.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying the operator returns the memory address of the variable/operand it is applied to, in any wording (e.g. 'the location of the variable in memory'). Part marks for vague answers such as 'an address' or 'a pointer' with no link to the operand. No marks if the student says it returns the value of the variable or the value pointed to (that is dereferencing).
